## What

Make session starts independent of cleanup, keep every existing cleanup running without overlapping host sweeps, and reuse branch-deletion decisions when their evidence is unchanged. A driver, the process that runs one plan’s tasks and closes when they finish, will finish maintenance only for the repository already in progress when it begins closing. Deliver both library fixes through the tools and engines this host actually runs.

## Why

The user said session startup “seems like it's taking a long time every time” and wanted results recorded “so it only has the rerun for each if something changed”. All 48 measured worker sessions started to do planned tasks since September 28 lost five minutes before starting; one sweep took 1,336 seconds and retired nothing. The user wants routine sweeps back to tens of seconds. After a finished run waited nearly eighteen minutes for maintenance, they also asked why a “background task” blocks completion and chose to stop it between repositories.

## Architecture

The ai-orchestrator repository owns one detached host job combining cleanup of old working directories, session records and temporary files. A lock shared across checkouts and worker worktrees prevents overlapping automatic and manual sweeps. Session starts can trigger it at most hourly and never wait. This fix can land independently of releases. The lock covers this combined job; onepipeline, the engine running planned work, still performs separate idle maintenance alongside it: cleanup between tasks, repository by repository. Safety when those passes meet belongs to onevcs.

The onevcs repository owns saved verdicts: decisions to keep or delete a branch together with the evidence behind them. They live separately from existing repository and session information, whose format stays unchanged so older engines can keep using it. Reversing reuse costs removing those saved decisions and the added report field, without converting shared state. Retention policy stays unchanged.

The onepipeline repository owns stopping maintenance between repositories, both during the pool pass, which maintains reusable working directories, and during the retirement pass, which deletes finished branches. It completes the current repository before closing and records the work left unvisited. It does not start a detached replacement; later idle passes and host sweeps handle remaining work. This commits report readers to an optional cut-short description on two existing records; reversing it costs removing that field and adjusting those readers. A single slow repository can still delay closing.

onepipeline must release an engine containing both its shutdown change and the improved onevcs. The onepipeline-ui repository must release its web service containing exactly that engine, since browser takeover runs its own engine. ai-orchestrator adopts matching tool releases together, including other versions that must agree. Delivery therefore depends on published packages from all three producer repositories; changing that arrangement would change the host’s agreement that installed tools and embedded engines match.

## Contracts

- Session setup launches cleanup without waiting or changing its own result. Automatic launches require no running sweep and no completion within the last hour. Manual sweeps take the same lock and report its holder and log when occupied. Both cleanup tools retain the four-hour age floor. Failures are logged and named on the next session start. A dry run, a sweep that only reports possible deletions and deletes nothing, neither needs nor updates the completion stamp.
- onevcs may reuse a verdict only when every input is unchanged: record and tool versions; repository and branch; the name and latest saved change of the branch it would merge into; where each local or remote copy of the branch is held and its latest saved change, including absence from the remote server; unreadable locations; recorded publication, landing and replacement evidence; rules for recognizing markers that record a merge; and any consulted change-request service answer. That service is asked afresh where needed. Missing, corrupt, incompatible or unreadable evidence requires fresh derivation; an unknown answer is never reusable.
- Reuse skips only the proof behind a verdict. Active users, exclusions, checked-out or dirty working directories and checks immediately before deletion stay fresh; deletion requires the branch still to have its expected commit. Saved decisions are written as complete replacements, including during dry runs. Interrupted or concurrent writers cannot leave a partial usable record; failure to save loses only the speed benefit. Existing repository and session formats and activity kinds remain unchanged.
- onevcs reports each examined decision through derivation: derived means worked out this time, reused means read from a valid saved verdict. A pass reads remote branch names and latest commits in bulk once per repository, except for fresh checks before deletion. It never repeats a commit-existence or ancestry question while its answer remains valid; fetching new commits invalidates negative existence answers.
- When its driver closes, onepipeline starts no further repository in either maintenance pass and finishes the current one completely, including safe branch deletion. The existing records for upkeep of reusable working directories (pool-maintenance) and deletion of finished branches (branches-retired) gain an optional description saying the pass was cut short because its run was closing and naming the repositories it never reached. The description is called cut_short, with reason driver-closing and a nonempty unreached list naming exactly those repositories, in visiting order. Completed work remains reported normally. A cut is recorded even when there is no other result; cutting the pool pass leaves every repository unreached in the retirement pass. Failed enumeration retains its existing error report. Fully visited passes keep their existing reports, with no new field or event kind. The results view explains the pool-maintenance cut and names the repositories left.
- The engine link change includes the shutdown change and waits for the published onevcs library; the web service waits for that engine library; host adoption waits for installable releases. The installed onevcs must match the engine’s copy, and the web service must contain exactly that engine. Adoption uses the plan’s supplied releases and never downgrades. The separate board-reads plan improves reading the task board and also updates the engine and web service, so it may install newer versions first. A version collision with that plan, or a changed shared contract, requires a manager ruling.

## Acceptance criteria

- Manager and worker session starts in any checkout or worktree finish within seconds despite a slow sweep, with all later setup steps and the correct exit result preserved. Concurrent automatic and manual host sweeps never overlap, and starts within an hour of completion launch none.
- The detached job still reclaims eligible working directories, session records and temporary files with the four-hour floor. Failed cleanup remains visible without failing session setup.
- Unchanged repeat passes reuse every examined verdict through both command-line entry points and the library the engine calls. They use bulk remote reads and no repeated proof work. Changed or unreadable inputs cannot authorize deletion using stale evidence; active use, exclusions, local changes and a new commit arriving before deletion remain protected. Concurrent and interrupted writes preserve complete usable records, and older supported tools still use shared state.
- A repeat sweep over several real test repositories with at least 150 candidate branches finishes within a measured bound of a few seconds, faster than the starting implementation. On this host, two consecutive dry-run sweep times are reported and the repeat is under 60 seconds, or a manager ruling on the slower measurement is recorded.
- A driver closing during either maintenance pass waits only for the repository in progress, with that repository’s work fully completed. Real-driver journeys over at least three repositories demonstrate the time bound and complete branch deletion; the run’s record of what happened identifies every unvisited repository and the results view explains the cut. Normal completed passes retain their previous reporting.
- The installed command-line tool, engine and web service contain the improved retirement code, and both engine copies contain the shutdown fix. A journey through the actual host sweep command reports the same nonempty set of kept and retirable branches twice: first derived, then reused. Installed package contents confirm matching versions; shared-state compatibility and documentation agree with the delivered behavior.
